research.title: LSEG CEO David Schwimmer on Where Global Capital Is Moving
research.summary: David Schwimmer, CEO of London Stock Exchange Group, explains why investors may be underestimating risks in today’s markets. In particular, Schwimmer says inflation and geopolitical tension limit the policy flexibility that has supported markets in past downturns. In conversation with FX de Mallmann, chairman of Goldman Sachs EMEA and chairman of Investment Banking, Schwimmer describes scenario planning as a more practical discipline than trying to predict what happens next.

research.title: The US Midterms: Reshaping the Stock Market
research.summary: The US midterm elections could strengthen the stock market rotation that was already underway, says Lou Miller, global head of Custom Basket Trading in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities. Traditional defensive sectors such as consumer staples are expensive right now, but healthcare stocks may provide defense along with earnings acceleration, Miller explains on The Markets podcast. He also says that stocks related to the data-center buildout have fallen sharply, resetting valuations and lowering the bar for positive surprises.

research.title: Why the Bond Market Remains Calm After the Blue Wave
research.summary: For investors, the U.S. election was only one part of a much bigger equation. Our Global Head of Fixed Income Andrew Sheets discusses the balance of risks after the midterm results. Read more insights from Morgan Stanley.
